paper_metadata.title: Quantum machine learning for quantum anomaly detection

experiments.description: Quantum kernel PCA anomaly detection for pure quantum states using a modified swap test to estimate centered-state overlaps and a proximity score.

algorithm.variant: Quantum kernel PCA for pure-state anomaly detection

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Training and test quantum states |psi_i> in a d-dimensional Hilbert space; centered states |z_i> are formed by subtracting the centroid state |psi_c>.

problem_instance.description: Semi-supervised anomaly detection on a training set of M unknown pure quantum states and one test state |psi0>.
problem_instance.dataset_size: M training states plus one test state

dataset_specification.description: No named dataset; states are assumed to be generated by quantum devices. The paper discusses generic pure states of dimension d.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Construct centroid state |psi_c>, centered states |z_i> and |z_0>, then estimate overlaps using a modified swap test.

quantum_resources.num_qubits: O(log d) for state registers; O(log M) additional label-register qubits in the logarithmic-in-M variant
quantum_resources.gate_count_total: O(log d) for state preparation subroutines; O(log M) Hadamard gates for centroid preparation

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Prepare centroid and centered states; estimate inner products via modified swap test with ancilla phase choices zeta=1 and zeta=i.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Combine estimated overlaps and normalization constants to compute f(psi0).

results.value: M training states plus one test state

speedup_claims.factor: logarithmic in d; logarithmic in M for pure states in the favorable protocol
speedup_claims.conditions: assuming access to state-preparation unitaries and modified swap tests; pure-state case with centroid-state preparation and low-rank/high-similarity assumptions for the O(log M) variant
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper does not report empirical accuracy; the speedup is asymptotic and resource-based. The O(log M) claim depends on additional assumptions and favorable state structure.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: O(poly(M log d)) for the direct overlap-estimation protocol; O(log M) resources for centroid-state preparation in the favorable low-rank/high-similarity setting

experiments.description: Quantum kernel PCA anomaly detection for pure quantum states using a superposition of centered data and a swap test to estimate the covariance-based proximity score.

algorithm.variant: Quantum kernel PCA for pure-state anomaly detection with centroid superposition

problem_formulation.encoding_details: The centered covariance operator C is encoded as the reduced density matrix of a superposition state |chi_c> over label and data registers.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate f(psi0) = 1 - tr(C) tr(C |z0><z0|) using a swap test between |z0> and C.

problem_instance.description: Same generic pure-state anomaly detection setting as the direct kernel PCA protocol, but using a different state-preparation route for the covariance matrix.
problem_instance.dataset_size: M training states plus one test state

dataset_specification.description: Generic unknown pure states |psi_i> and |psi0> of dimension d.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Prepare centered states and the superposition |chi_c> whose partial trace yields C.

quantum_resources.num_qubits: O(log d) for state registers; O(log M) for label register in state preparation
quantum_resources.gate_count_total: O(log M) Hadamard gates for label superposition; O(log d) for state preparation

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Generate |chi_c> and reduced covariance matrix C from centered training states.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Use swap-test probabilities to estimate the anomaly score.

results.value: M training states plus one test state

speedup_claims.factor: logarithmic in d after covariance preparation
speedup_claims.conditions: once the covariance operator C is prepared as a reduced density matrix; swap-test evaluation of the anomaly score
speedup_claims.caveats: No empirical benchmark is reported. The O(log d) claim applies to the evaluation stage, not necessarily the full end-to-end preparation cost.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: O(log d) for the swap-test evaluation once C is prepared; state preparation uses O(log M) resources

experiments.description: Quantum one-class SVM anomaly detection for pure quantum states using pairwise fidelity estimation and classical matrix inversion.

algorithm.variant: Quantum one-class SVM for pure states, swap-test-based kernel estimation

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Quantum states |psi_i> are compared pairwise via swap test to build the kernel matrix K.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Solve (K + PT M 1) alpha = e and compute f(psi0) = |sum_i alpha_i |<psi_i|psi_0>|^2 - 1|.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: One-class SVM threshold handled through PT; restricted formulation sets r = 1.

problem_instance.description: Generic pure-state one-class classification/anomaly detection on M training states and one test state.
problem_instance.dataset_size: M training states plus one test state

dataset_specification.description: No named dataset; generic quantum states of dimension d.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Estimate all pairwise fidelities |<psi_i|psi_j>|^2 and solve the linear system for alpha.

quantum_resources.num_qubits: O(log d) per swap-test fidelity estimate; O(log M) qubits for the HHL-based variant
quantum_resources.gate_count_total: O(M^2 log d) total for pairwise fidelity estimation in the direct protocol; O(log M) runtime for HHL subroutine in the idealized variant

implementation_details.classical_solver: Classical matrix inversion for the direct protocol; HHL for the quantum linear-system variant
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Compute pairwise fidelities via swap tests; assemble kernel matrix K.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Invert the linear system to obtain alpha and evaluate the anomaly score on the test state.

results.value: M training states plus one test state

speedup_claims.factor: polynomial / logarithmic in M for the idealized HHL-based variant
speedup_claims.baseline_method: classical matrix inversion after kernel estimation
speedup_claims.conditions: requires HHL assumptions, low-rank kernel matrix, efficient state preparation, and condition number 1/PT <= O(log M)
speedup_claims.caveats: The direct protocol is not a speedup in M because it still requires O(M^2) kernel estimation and O(M^3) classical inversion. The O(log M) claim is idealized.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: Direct protocol: O(M^2 log d) for kernel estimation plus O(M^3) classical inversion; idealized HHL-based variant: O(log M) for matrix inversion under stated assumptions
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: O(M^3) for matrix inversion after kernel estimation

experiments.description: Quantum one-class SVM anomaly detection for pure quantum states using HHL matrix inversion, quantum PCA-style kernel exponentiation, and modified swap tests to evaluate the final proximity score.

algorithm.variant: Quantum one-class SVM with HHL-based matrix inversion and quantum PCA kernel simulation

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Training states are loaded into a superposition |chi> = (1/sqrt(M)) sum_i |i>|psi_i>; the kernel matrix is represented as a density matrix.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Solve (K + PT M 1) alpha = e via HHL and compute f(psi0) = |sum_i alpha_i |<psi_i|psi_0>|^2 - 1|.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Threshold acceptance probability PT acts as regularization/constraint parameter; r fixed to 1.

problem_instance.description: Generic pure-state one-class SVM anomaly detection with low-rank kernel matrix assumptions.
problem_instance.dataset_size: M training states plus one test state

dataset_specification.description: No named dataset; generic quantum states of dimension d.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Prepare |chi> from the controlled unitary UC; build K0 from partial trace; simulate exp(-iKt) using modified quantum PCA; generate |phi1> and |phi2> for the final overlap test.

quantum_resources.num_qubits: O(log M) for HHL and label registers, plus O(log d) for state registers
quantum_resources.gate_count_total: O(log M) runtime for HHL under ideal assumptions; exp(-iKt) simulation uses 2n copies of K0 and error O(t^2/n)
quantum_resources.num_shots: O(1/epsilon^2) measurements for the final modified swap test

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Prepare the uniform superposition, load training states via UC, estimate kernel matrix K0, and perform HHL to obtain alpha.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Use modified swap tests on |phi1> and |phi2> to estimate Re and Im of their overlap and compute the anomaly score.

results.value: M training states plus one test state

results.unit: qubits for HHL and label registers
measurements for final modified swap test

speedup_claims.baseline_method: classical one-class SVM with matrix inversion and kernel evaluation
speedup_claims.conditions: idealized HHL-based matrix inversion, efficient kernel simulation via quantum PCA-style method, low-rank kernel matrix, and condition number requirement 1/PT <= O(log M)
speedup_claims.caveats: This is a theoretical resource estimate, not an empirical benchmark. The kernel simulation itself requires multiple copies of K0 and incurs O(t^2/n) error.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: Idealized O(log M) matrix inversion plus O(log M) overlap-estimation repetitions under the paper's assumptions; kernel simulation error O(t^2/n)

experiments.description: Quantum anomaly detection for mixed quantum states using a mixed-state kernel PCA analogue and a generalized overlap estimation procedure based on Kraus operators.

algorithm.variant: Quantum kernel PCA for mixed-state anomaly detection

hyperparameters.proximity_measure: Eq. (23) mixed-state analogue of pure-state kernel PCA score

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Mixed states rho_k are defined by Kraus operators E_l^(k) acting on |0><0|; anomaly score is built from pairwise mixed-state overlaps.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Compute f(rho0) from mixed-state overlap terms and normalization constants, reducing to the pure-state kernel PCA score in the pure-state limit.

problem_instance.description: Generic anomaly detection on M mixed quantum states and one test mixed state.
problem_instance.dataset_size: M training density matrices plus one test density matrix

dataset_specification.description: No named dataset; density matrices rho_i are represented via Kraus operators.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Estimate mixed-state overlaps using a generalized ancilla-based procedure with controlled Kraus operations.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Prepare ancilla plus system state, apply controlled Kraus operations E^(k,i), and estimate real/imaginary parts of mixed-state overlaps.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Assemble the mixed-state proximity score from estimated overlap terms.

results.value: M training density matrices plus one test density matrix

speedup_claims.conditions: assuming access to controlled Kraus operations and the generalized overlap-estimation procedure
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper does not provide empirical results. The stated complexity is O(poly(M log d)), so the speedup is primarily in the Hilbert-space dimension, not necessarily in M.

experiments.description: Quantum anomaly detection for mixed quantum states using a superfidelity kernel and a one-class SVM-style proximity score.

algorithm.variant: Quantum one-class SVM for mixed states using superfidelity kernel

hyperparameters.kernel: superfidelity F(rho_i, rho_j) = tr(rho_i rho_j) + sqrt(1-tr(rho_i^2)) sqrt(1-tr(rho_j^2))

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Mixed-state kernel matrix is built from the superfidelity between density matrices rho_i and rho_j.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Compute f(rho0) = |sum_i alpha_i F_i0(rho_i, rho_0) - 1|^2 after solving the corresponding linear system for alpha.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Same one-class SVM thresholding as the pure-state case; no access to UC required in the direct protocol.
